To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of anti-neutrinos in a long-baseline neutrinos experiment is possible; (2) the resulting sensitivity is comparable to that of a neutrino and anti neutrino run with the same beam; (3) the use of a Gadolinium-loaded water Cerenkov is possible; (4) the use of Gadolinium improves sensitivity by a factor of 5;
a long baseline neutrinos from muon decays at rest can be used to study CP violation and θ 13 in neutrino oscillation physics.

the use of low energy antineutrinos from muons decaying at rest in a gadolinium-loaded water Čerenkov detector, allows to increase the sensitivity of a long baseline experiment for the determination of the leptonic CP violation phase by a factor 2.5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of the neutrino and the search for new physics.
a novel method to measure neutrino oscillations.
the possibility to use anti-neutrino from muon decay-at-rest for a long-baseline neutrinos oscillation experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a neutrino factory is the best solution to study neutrino oscillations.

a DUNE-like experiment with a muon decaying at rest neutrino beam would have the ability to measure all of the neutrino parameters of interest with a factor of two to three better sensitivity than a conventional experiment with the same beam energy.
the DUNE experiment, with its large mass of liquid argon and its long baseline to Fermilab, is the best option to discover CP violation and measure the mass hierarchy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this approach can be used to improve the discovery reaches of the mass hierarchy, CP violation and θ 13.

this approach can greatly improve the sensitivity of the long-baseline experiments to the unknowns of the lepton flavor sector, while maintaining the ability to measure CP violation and the mass hierarchy.
this approach is a good alternative for the anti-neutrinos running in the next generation long baseline neutrino experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of low-energy neutrinos from decay at rest allows a significant increase in the number of anti-neutrino events in a long-baseline neutrinos experiment, and that this approach is complementary to the conventional superbeam approach.
anti-neutrinos are a valuable resource for neutrino oscillation physics and should not be ignored.
the use of anti-neutrinos in the decay at rest mode is competitive, if not superior to the conventional anti-neutrino mode for the study of neutrino oscillation physics.
